COUNTY PALATINE OF CHESTER. BYE-LAWS for providing Rear Lights on Vehicles using the Streets, Highways or Roads in the ADMINISTRATIVE COUNTY OF CHESTER (excepting the Municipal Boroughs situate therein). NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Cheshire County Council, at a Meeting held at Chester Castle, on Thursday, the Ist day of August, 1912, made under Section 5 (3) of the Lights on Vehicles Act, 1907, the following BYE-LAWS, viz. : REAR LIGHTS ON 17(JIICLES 1. (1) Every person who shall cause or permit any vehicle to be in any street, highway, or road, to which the public have access, during the period between one hour after sunset and one hour before sunrise, besides complying with requirements of the lights on Vehicles Act, 1907, shall provide such vehicle either (a) with a lamp (or lamps) in proper working order, and so con- structed and capable of being so attached as when lighted to show to the rear a red light visible for a reasonable distance ; or (b) with a reflector (or reflectors) at least inches wide, so constructed and capable of being so attached to such vehicle as to reflect a red light from a light carried by a vehicle approaching from behind. If only one lamp or reflector is provided, it shall be placed on the off or right side of the vehicle, or if such vehicle is used for the purpose of drawing behind it any other vehicle or load, on the off or right side of such other vehicle or load. (2) Every person driving or being in charge of such vehicle in any street, highway or road, to which the public have access during the period as aforesaid, shall keep such lamp or lamps properly attached and properly trimmed and lighted or such reflector or reflectors properly attached and in such condition as to reflect a red light. DEFINITION. 2. The expression" vehicle "in these Bye-laws shall mean every vehicle machine or implement to which the Lights on Vehicles Act, 1907, applies. EXTENT AND COMMENCEMENT OF BYE-LAWS 3. These Bye-laws shall have effect and be in force in the whole of the Administrative County of Chester, except in such parts as are comprised within any Municipal Borough, and shall come into force on the Ist day of January, 1913. PENALTY. 4. If any person offends against these Bye•laws he shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding Forty Shillings, and in the case of a second or subsequent con- viction to a penalty not exceeding Five Pounds. Pro- vided that if a person driving or being in charge of a vehicle is charged with an offence against these Bye- laws, he shall not be convicted thereof if he proves to the satisfaction of the Court that such offence arose through the neglect or default of some other person whose duty it was to provide the vehicle with a lamp or lamps or reflector or reflectors. AND NOTICE IS HEREBY FURTHER GIVEN that a sealed copy of such Bye-laws has been for- warded to the Secretary of State. REGINALD POTTS, Clerk to the Cheshire County Council. Chester, 2nd Aneust, 1912.

J Finch (Penketh) struggled manfully against A Gleave, who had the remarkable lead of 19-7 at the 20th end. Finch then got the little 'un and ran in eight successive singles up to the 30th end when the Literal gained his last wood and won by seven points. The per- formance of the villager was really a fine one and he did exceedingly well. -- W Taylor (Liberal) and H Bowyer (Penketh) were evenly matched and played well together all through the game and alter many interesting lengths the score was 19 each at the 29th end. Taylor got a good couple on the next lorgth to win by 21-19. -- .I Bowyer and F Walker (liberal) played a good game and front the first to the 19th end the Liberal had a slight lead which however was soon dealt with by the villager who had 17-13 at the 22nd end. Walker settled down again and after peeling with 17 at the 28th end he ran his score to 19-11. Bowyer got two neat singles and peeled with 19 but the Liberal was well on the jac.{ and got his wincing two on the next end. -- Having led from the first to the 23rd end, E Ashton (Penketn) seemed to be well on the way to being the only villager with a winning card, but the Liberal was all there, and after hAving peeled with 16 at tho 2.lth end Smith eventually won by three points. The Liberals thoroughly deserve their victory, and the villagers have a lot to aipe off to-day, and we should be surprised if the Liberals did not cows back with a win. 11..tiough it will not be such a big one, for the Penlosthites area good lot on their own award. -- WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT ASSOCIATION.
